newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: It was a hectic day in the South African debt market as bonds surged on an unexpected fall in first quarter Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth but stopped short of a major technical break on the downside.
At 1415 GMT government's key R150 loan yielded 14.875 percent from a morning best of 14.84 percent and 15.06 percent in after-hours trade on Wednesday.
"All hell broke lose after the GDP figures at 0730 GMT," is how one debt trader described the morning flurry.
GDP fell a seasonally adjusted and annualised 0.8 percent in the quarter to March after rising 3.3 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996. Economists had, on average, forecast a 2.5 percent rise.
The debt market was cheered by speculation that the weak growth numbers would put pressure on the Reserve Bank to lower currently high interest rates in order to stimulate the economy.
"The figure was seen supporting an interest rate cut," a senior trader at a big bank said.
"But there is still a lot of water to flow under the bridge (until an interest rate cut). The intraday trend was down but the question is whether it is sustainable," she added.
UAL Merchant Bank Treasury analyst Boyde Stafne said a downside break of 14.84 percent was critical from a technical perspective and would "divide the bulls from the bears."
The GDP release followed a mixed set of economic numbers on Wednesday which showed higher-than-expected inflation and credit numbers but broadly-based M3 money supply growth easing.
On Friday, the key question would be whether the market could close below 14.84 percent on follow-through buying, debt traders said.
"It's crucial to break the (14.84 percent) level on a daily and weekly basis because it shows that we would have broken out of the current bear channel," one said.
Some upbeat traders forecast a 14.81 to 14.95 percent trading range for the day.
Foreigners were net sellers of 109.19 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Wednesday after selling 458.79 million rand's worth on Tuesday, the Bond Exchange said.
Wednesday's nominal exchange turnover was 4.95 billion rand from 5.92 billion rand on Tuesday.
The rand also had a more cheerful day, firming against a higher U.S. dollar which benefitted from an asset revalue row between the German Bundesbank and government.
At 1415 GMT the rand was at 4.4670/4700 to the dollar from 4.4710/4740 overnight.
The gains came on the back of a large London dollar sell order which hit the local market in the morning and continued to be transacted throughout the day, forex traders said.
"We saw some export dollars but it was mainly a big London dollar sell order," a senior forex trader said.
He said the market was generally long on dollars and players would likely cut positions on Friday, capping any further gains beyond the 4.4650 level.
The unit was seen moving in the established 4.46 to 4.48 range on Friday with no major blips.
In cross rate action, the rand was last changing hands at 0.3796/3800 to the mark from 0.3790/3793 late on Tuesday.
The local unit was trading at 25.9441/9839 yen from 25.7909/8194 yen previously and 7.3214/3308 to the British pound from 7.3233/3327 before.
Three-month NCD rates remained unchanged from Friday at 16.35 percent offered, as did 90-day BA rates which lined up at 15.85 percent.
South Africa's money market shortage edged lower to 6.491 billion rand on Wednesday from 6.780 billion rand on Tuesday, the Reserve Bank said.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482-1003
